fig2_1: Line plot of temperature u versus position x on the interval zero to two pi, overlaying the heat equation solution at several increasing times. The initial curve is a sharp triangle wave peaking at x equals pi; as time grows the corner rounds off and successive curves flatten toward the constant equilibrium value pi over two, showing that high-frequency modes (decaying like e to the power minus n squared t) vanish fastest.
fig2_2: Three-dimensional waterfall surface of the heat equation solution u over the space axis x and the time axis t. The front edge is the sharp triangle wave; moving back in time the ridges smooth and collapse rapidly to a flat plateau at the mean value pi over two, visualizing exponential decay of the higher-frequency Fourier modes and the diffusive smoothing of the initial corner.
fig2_3: Line plot of string displacement u versus position x on zero to pi, showing the vibrating-string solution at several times across half a period. Starting from the triangular plucked shape, the curves shrink and pass through the flat axis, then grow into the inverted mirror-image triangle at t equals T over two, with amplitude conserved rather than decaying, illustrating undamped oscillation with period two pi.
fig2_4: Three-dimensional waterfall surface of the wave equation solution u over position x and time t spanning one full period. The triangular plucked profile sweeps back and forth between its initial shape and its inverted mirror image without any loss of amplitude, the repeating ridges showing periodic, energy-conserving oscillation in contrast to the decaying heat solution.
fig2_5: Two-dimensional color or contour map of the harmonic function u over the periodic strip, with horizontal axis x from zero to two pi and vertical axis y from zero to one. At the bottom boundary y equals zero the field reproduces the boundary data, a sine wave plus a smaller, higher-frequency triple-sine ripple; moving upward the pattern decays to zero at y equals one, with the n equals three component damping out much faster than the n equals one component, demonstrating harmonic smoothing into the interior.
